judged_text: The existing-attendee dedup compares emails case-sensitively (guest === attendee.email) while guest emails are stored verbatim (line 86), so a case variant of an existing attendee is not filtered out. A caller re-adds alice@x.com as Alice@X.com, creating a second attendee row for the same real mailbox — the person is double-counted on the booking, receives duplicate emails, and appears twice on the calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing-attendee de-dupe is `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and new attendee rows are created with `email: guest` (no normalization). Since neither side is lowercased/trimmed, `alice@x.com` vs `Alice@X.com` will bypass the filter and be inserted via `createMany`, leading to duplicate attendee rows/emails/calendar entries for the same mailbox. (Blacklist is lowercased but compared against unlowercased `guest` too.)
